A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GePBench and support a reliable comparison of text, algorithms, tables, and figures. All 12 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2 were inspected; v1 ends with references, while v2 includes Appendices A–F. Revised datasets and settings require caution when comparing scores directly.

before.justification: V1 reports original MLLM evaluations, visual-encoder experiments, shape-count analyses, and downstream results for LLaVA-GeP.

after.justification: V2 reports revised model and transfer results, plus original human evaluation, answer-parser validation, and controlled noise experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same shape sampling, relationship generation, and overlap filtering steps. The template-based benchmark and two-stage LLaVA-GeP training approach remain intact. Expanded rendering, architecture, captioning, and LoRA descriptions document implementation details without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 retains v1's nine general transfer benchmarks and adds MME, LLaVA-Wild, MATH-Vision, MathVerse, MathVista, CharXiv, ChartQA, and ChartBench (Figure 6; Appendix D.3). Dedicated mathematical reasoning and chart interpretation substantially broaden evaluated task coverage. The additional benchmarks in Figure 7 provide a literature-sourced comparison, not evidence of fresh evaluations on all those datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces LLaVA-NeXT 7B/34B/72B with LLaVA-OneVision 7B/72B and introduces a measured human reference, adding an important comparison group. Figure 5 also changes participation, expanding from five to fourteen models while removing Mantis-Idefics2. The encoder configurations in Table 2 and the LLaVA-1.5 transfer baseline remain.

E3.justification: The reported benchmark changes from 20K images/250K questions to 80K/285K, with revised distributions. V2 replaces v1's 300K instruction-training description with a stratified 240K set and adds human-study and paired noise/no-noise protocols. Zero-shot evaluation, temperature 0, 640x640 inputs, and accuracy remain. The exact revised question count is inconsistent: Figure 3 totals 315,640 rather than the stated 285K.

E4.justification: V2 adds a controlled noise ablation holding questions and underlying figures fixed (Appendix E.2), a manual parsing audit of 100 responses per model (Appendix B.2), and cross-benchmark human–model gap analysis (Section 4.4). Shape-count analysis expands. The existing encoder ablation remains; its detailed discussion moves to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. V2's participant and audit sample counts describe evaluation designs; results still use point estimates without new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise size scores and resulting averages extensively, while corresponding non-size scores remain unchanged. For example, GPT-4o easy-size accuracy changes from 23.3% to 17.5%, and Gemini hard-size accuracy from 68.1% to 44.4%. V2 adds 99.3% human accuracy, noise and parser findings, and new transfer results; retained transfer scores also change. Revised corpus and training descriptions prevent interpreting these as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and Algorithm 1's mathematical procedure is unchanged. V2's additional task-generation and performance-gap descriptions do not introduce substantive formal definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that GePBench evaluates neglected fundamental geometric perception, current MLLMs struggle with it, and geometric training data improves downstream multimodal capabilities. V2's human measurements and quantified math/chart gains support these retained contributions rather than establish a different central claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds an encoder-invariance explanation for spatial failures and training-distribution explanations for models benefiting from noise. It qualifies cross-benchmark gaps when GPT-4V substitutes for GPT-4o. V1's VizWiz unanswerable-question attribution and mixed-encoder gap-narrowing interpretation disappear. These substantially revise the explanatory discussion, although the formal limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D add checkpoint identifiers, collection dates, evaluation prompts, answer parsing, captioner/judge identity, training-data assembly, hyperparameters, LoRA information, GPU counts, and training times. V2 also discloses noise probability and the shape-count difficulty threshold. These materially improve implementation documentation; both versions still promise future release of GePBench code and data.

R1.justification: V2 substantially extends positioning through comparisons with human–model gaps on benchmarks including BLINK, CODIS, and HR-Bench, alongside additional math/chart literature. It adds visual-invariance references supporting its mechanism discussion and replaces the LLaVA-NeXT citation with OneVision. Matplotlib and Perlin references also replace v1's empty citation placeholders.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and dataset-construction narrative are extensively rewritten, emphasizing foundational perception versus high-level semantics. Detailed task descriptions and encoder discussion move into appendices with summaries in the main text. New human-comparison sections and reorganized transfer discussion substantially change the document's structure.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 are redrawn or substantially reformatted, including rearranged examples, a compact pipeline, reordered distributions, and revised plot axes and legends. V1's downstream Table 3 becomes expanded radar plots in v2 Figure 6. Human-gap, prompt, noise, and source displays are added. The redesigned Figure 1 introduces an answer-letter mismatch: circumscribed is option C but the answer says B.

improvement.justification: V2 supports v1's asserted human competence with measured results, adds controlled noise and parser validation, broadens transfer evidence, and substantially improves reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by newly inconsistent benchmark accounting: Figure 3 totals 315,640 questions against 285K stated, whereas v1's counts supported approximately 250K. The new Figure 1 answer-letter error further weakens reporting precision. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
